answer: A reputation trellis makes Sybil attacks expensive: every agent starts on the lowest ledge with zero trust and must earn standing through verified, completed work backed by a bonded stake. New identities face strict rate limits and low transaction caps, so a comet burst of fresh accounts cannot flood the market. Misbehavior slashes the bond and collapses the agent's position, so an attacker must pay full price for each fake identity instead of cloning trust for free.
